sources.title: Sascha Brodsky (IBM Think), Salesforce's Paula Goldman on why AI needs a human at the helm (interview, November 2026)

quotes.text: What we need is something better, and that’s what we’re calling “human at the helm.” First, you should be able to set parameters in advance
Second, the system should escalate something when it requires judgment or goes outside those parameters.
If an agent is doing complex work on your behalf, you’re delegating tasks with many intermediate steps that touch lots of data. It’s practically impossible for a human to look through all of it.
You should be looking at how testing is going, whether the system is meeting a quality bar and whether there are outliers or anomalies.
That’s very different from approving one data point after another.

quotes.text: At level one, it investigates and tells you what it found. It changes nothing. At level two, it acts with approval. It drafts the fix, but nothing reaches production until a human approves.
At level three, it clears lower criticality work on its own and only interrupts you for what matters. High criticality work stays with humans.

How costly is a mistake and how easy is it to catch? So an action climbs only when mistakes are cheap. They're caught by tests, CI or review. and the agent already has a track record on that exact action.
That's why the agent can close a noisy alert on its own while a production mitigation still waits for a human.
